fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` and
`src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` declare `trace_id` as `["string","null"]`,
described as "Langfuse trace id when tracing is enabled", but `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`
hardcodes `None` at every site emitting it. No per-run identity exists, so a verdict cannot name
its run and no header can carry a run-stable value.

## Approach

Mint one identity per gate run at the two boundaries that already resolve the run's config
exactly once: `workflow/gate_dispatch.py:167` (plan-review, `ctx.ticket_id` in scope) and `:762`
(completion-verifier, `ticket_id` in scope). Both open `gate_config(cfg)`, whose contextvar every
op reads via `resolve_gate_config` (`config.py:99-107`). Attach with
`dataclasses.replace(cfg, ...)` before `gate_config(cfg)`, never mutating the caller's object.

Three values: `trace_id` (32 lowercase hex from `secrets.token_hex(16)`), `ticket_id` (the
boundary's own), `operation` (`"review-plan"` or `"verify-completion"`, rebar's canonical verb names, so the
header vocabulary matches the CLI and docs rather than inventing a second spelling). No `run_id` —
`trace_id` already identifies the run. `ticket_id` and `operation` are minted here because the
boundary is the only place they are knowable; their consumer is the delivery ticket's
`${run:...}` vocabulary (`26ae-041f-dcc4-4279`), and criteria below cover them so they are
verifiable now rather than resting on that follow-on.

The 32-hex shape matches W3C trace-id format, so later work can supply a real OpenTelemetry
trace id with no schema or format migration. Random per run, not derived from the ticket: a
derived value would merge every re-review into one trace, and the verdict's own `trace_id`
already leads back from a verdict to its run.

The value reaches pool workers unchanged: both plan-review pools submit through
`generation._submit_ctx` — `ex.submit(contextvars.copy_context().run, fn, *args)`
(`generation.py:154-165`), used by `pass1.py:426-427` and `container_stage.py:260`.

Read `req.config.trace_id` at **all three** `runner.py` sites that hardcode `None`:

- `:254` — `FakeRunner.run`'s `mode == "structured"` branch, comment "Structured mode (e.g.
  verify_completion)". The completion verifier is structured-mode, so its fake verdict returns
  here, not `:259`; omitting it makes the completion criterion below unsatisfiable.
- `:259` — `FakeRunner.run`'s findings branch.
- `:719` — the real runner.

The two `FakeRunner` branches are selected by `req.mode`, so testing one says nothing about the
other. The seam is `req.config`, not a runner attribute: the resolved gate config arrives as
`RunRequest(config=...)` (`operations.py:209-212`), and `FakeRunner` holds no instance config,
already reaching configuration only through `req.config` (`req.config.repo_path` at `:264`).
`max_output_cfg` and similar per-request derivations use `dataclasses.replace`, so the identity
rides through unchanged.

Both schema descriptions are restated in the same change so the contract cannot contradict the
emitted value. The wording is "per-gate-run correlation id (32 lowercase hex); null for
deterministic or fallback verdicts and standalone ops" — deliberately **not** "present inside any
gate run". Other emitters run inside a gate scope with no LLM call
(`workflow/completion_verdict_assembly.py:153`, `completion_reconcile.py:252`,
`workflow/completion_failures.py:98`), and `spec_scan.py:138` is not a gate op; all stay `None`
and are out of scope, because a deterministic verdict has no gateway request behind it and
naming a trace there would imply traffic that does not exist.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py` — the identity fields on `LLMConfig`.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — mint at both run boundaries.
- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py` — read `req.config.trace_id` at `:254`, `:259`, `:719`.
- `src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `src/rebar/schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json` — restate the `trace_id` description.
- `tests/unit/test_run_correlation.py` (new) — the tests below.

## Testing

Tier: in-process unit tests plus schema validation. The mechanism is contextvar propagation and
verdict field population, both of which run for real in-process; no subprocess or network
boundary is involved.

- Happy path: within one scope every `resolve_gate_config()` read returns the same `trace_id`.
- Edge: two scopes differ; the value is `None` outside any gate run.
- Concurrency: a value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's,
  exercising the real `copy_context()` seam rather than asserting on it structurally.
- Real-runner path: `:719` driven through `PydanticAIRunner.run` with the offline
  `model_override` TestModel harness, so the real finalize path runs with no network call. Every
  other verdict assertion is satisfiable through `FakeRunner`, which would leave `:719` unproven.
- Both gate surfaces: plan-review and completion-verifier each produce a verdict carrying the
  run's `trace_id`, validated against its own schema. Testing one side would leave half the
  changed surface unverified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Inside one gate run `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` is identical across repeated reads;
      checked by asserting equality across three reads in one scope.
- [ ] Two gate runs produce different `trace_id` values; checked by a test over two scopes.
- [ ] `trace_id` is 32 lowercase hex; checked by `re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", value)`.
- [ ] A value read inside a `_submit_ctx` pool task equals the submitting thread's; checked by
      submitting a reader through the real `_submit_ctx`.
- [ ] Within a gate scope `resolve_gate_config().ticket_id` and `.operation` equal what the
      boundary minted them from, with `operation` equal to `review-plan` and `verify-completion`
      respectively; checked by asserting both, for each boundary.
- [ ] A plan-review verdict carries the run's `trace_id` and validates against
      `review_result.schema.json`; checked by asserting the field and running the validator.
- [ ] A completion-verifier verdict produced in a completion-verifier scope carries that run's
      `trace_id` and validates against `completion_verdict.schema.json`; checked by asserting the
      field equals `resolve_gate_config().trace_id` and running the validator.
- [ ] A verdict produced through the real runner site `:719` carries `req.config.trace_id`;
      checked by driving `PydanticAIRunner.run` in a gate scope with the offline `model_override`
      TestModel harness, so no `FakeRunner` branch can satisfy it.
- [ ] Both schema descriptions state the per-gate-run correlation id in 32-hex shape and the
      deterministic/fallback exemption, with no residual Langfuse claim and no "present inside
      any gate run" wording; checked by a grep over both files.
- [ ] A deterministic completion verdict produced inside a gate scope still carries
      `trace_id: null`; checked by driving the deterministic child-closure path.
- [ ] The identity survives a per-request config derivation; checked by asserting
      `max_output_cfg(cfg).trace_id == cfg.trace_id`.
- [ ] Outside any gate run the identity is `None` and verdicts are unchanged; checked by
      asserting `trace_id is None` for a standalone op.
